editorial:
Imagine trying to put on a huge Broadway show while the entire world is shutting down. That is exactly what you get with this look at the revival of Company. You get to follow director Marianne Elliott as she takes a classic musical and flips it on its head by swapping the genders of the main characters. It feels like you are right there in the rehearsal room, watching the cast struggle and succeed. The vibe is very inspiring and honest, showing you that making art is often messy and stressful, especially when you are dealing with a global pandemic in New York City.

What really makes this shine is seeing the raw footage of the actors getting into character. Watching legends like Patti LuPone and the genius Stephen Sondheim himself talk about their work is a huge treat. The pacing is steady, though some might find the deep dives into theater history a bit slow. If you love music or just like seeing how things are made behind the scenes, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the actual opening night of the show. You see all the hard work pay off as the curtain rises and the audience cheers. It ends with a heartfelt look at how the theater community survived the pandemic together. The final scenes emphasize that art helps people heal after a crisis, leaving you feeling happy and hopeful as the credits roll over the final performance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Broadway, music, or seeing how creative projects come to life.
